answer: Each agent earns a reputation token that decays from zenith to nadir unless refreshed by independent vouchers. When a voucher vouches for a newcomer it must also maintain a live escrow that drops into a canyon of penalties if the vouchee is later proven a duplicate, forcing the voucher to pay the escrow plus a network fee. An attacker therefore must acquire dozens of trusted vouchers, each costing token stakes and time, making large‑scale Sybil attacks economically prohibitive.
